The captioned writ petition is filed seeking direction against respondent No.1 - The Deputy
Commissioner & Arbitrator to pass final orders/Award in respect of lands, which are acquired by the
National Highway Authorities.

sentences.text: 3 NC: 2026:KHC:13870 HC-KAR 3

. The grievance of the petitioners before this Court is that respondent No.2 - the Special Land Acquisition Officer has passed an award determining compensation at the rate of 840/- per square meter for dry lands and 924/- per square meter for wet lands.

Being dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation determined under the award, the petitioners have invoked the remedy available under Section 3G(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956 and approached respondent No.1 - the Deputy Commissioner, who is functioning as the Arbitrator.
The principal grievance of the petitioners is that though their arguments were addressed before the Arbitrator in July 2025, no final order has been passed till date.

4. On perusal of the records, this Court finds that if the petitioners had concluded their arguments in July 2025, respondent No.1 - the Deputy Commissioner and Arbitrator ought not to indefinitely defer the adjudication of the claim without justifiable reasons.
The petitioners have admittedly lost their lands pursuant to acquisition NC: 2026:KHC:13870 HC-KAR proceedings initiated under the National Highways Act.
Once the lands are acquired and the petitioners are divested of their immovable property, their right to seek fair and reasonable compensation assumes significance.
Though the right to property is no longer a fundamental right, it remains a constitutional right protected under Article 300A of the Constitution of India.
Therefore, the petitioners are entitled to seek just and reasonable compensation for the lands acquired.
When the petitioners are aggrieved by the award passed by the Special Land Acquisition Officer, the statute provides an efficacious remedy under Section 3G(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956.
Consequently, respondent No.1 - the Deputy Commissioner and Arbitrator is under a statutory obligation to examine the grievance relating to the quantum of compensation determined in the award.

In the present case, despite the petitioners having concluded their arguments in July 2025, the absence of a final decision demonstrates inaction on the part of the NC: 2026:KHC:13870 HC-KAR Arbitrator, thereby justifying the petitioners in seeking appropriate directions from this Court in the nature of a writ of mandamus.

5. For the foregoing reasons, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The writ petition is allowed.

(ii) Respondent No.1 - the Deputy Commissioner and Arbitrator is directed to pass final orders, in accordance with law, within an outer limit of two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this order.

Sd/-
(SACHIN SHANKAR MAGADUM) JUDGE NBM List No.: 2 Sl No.: 20 Narayanaswamy S R vs The Deputy Commissioner on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24670901/
